matches: - path: type: PathPrefix value: / filters: - type: ExternalAuth externalAuth: protocol: HTTP backendRef: name: authentik-server namespace: authentik port: 80 http: path: /outpost.goauthentik.io/auth/envoy allowedHeaders: - signal.title: docs: document Envoy listener redirect and wildcard port in L4 policy
signal.text: Add a section to the Layer 4 policy docs covering the toPorts listener field, which redirects matching egress traffic to a named Envoy listener defined in a CiliumEnvoyConfig or CiliumClusterwideEnvoyConfig. Includes three examples: a header-injection redirect, an external forward proxy with Proxy-Authorization, and a wildcard-port (port 0) variant that redirects all internet-bound egress. Documents the egress-only and no-L7-rules constraints, the use-original-source-address annotation, built-in egress-cluster routing, credential handling limits, and recommends Gateway API/GAMMA for cases they cover. Cross-links the L7 traffic management page. ```release-note docs: document Envoy listener redirect and wildcard port in L4 policy ``` cc @jrajahalme

signal.title: cilium-cli: bump test-connection-disruption image to v0.0.18
signal.text: Bumps the conn-disrupt test image to pick up cilium/test-connection-disruption#19, which makes the TCP client honour `--timeout` for its write deadline instead of a hardcoded one second. Only the reader honoured `--timeout`, so a write stall of just over a second ended the client with `conn write: write tcp ...: i/o timeout` and failed `no-interrupted-connections` on a restart count mismatch during an e2e-upgrade downgrade. This PR was prepared with AIL:3.

signal.title: CFP: Make fixed (reserved/well known) identities granular per cluster for Cluster Mesh
signal.text: ## Cilium Feature Proposal **Is your proposed feature related to a problem?** Currently, all Cilium identities with a fixed numeric identity are in the 0-256 range **regardless of their cluster**. This mostly means the reserved identities, but also the well-known ones (well-known identities are disabled by default and do not seem to have a lot of usage though). As a result, we essentially accept CiliumEndpoint(Slice) objects from remote clusters with identities in the 0-256 range and users can not have per cluster granularity. The most problematic consequence of this is for the ingress identity/entity. A NetworkPolicy accepting traffic from ingress necessarily accepts traffic from all connected clusters. This means that a user in a connected cluster who can create ingress/Gateway API resources (or anything else that makes traffic act as the ingress identity) could theoretically circumvent some network policies if they allow traffic from the ingress identity. **Describe the feature you'd like** Change all reserved/well-known identities to use each cluster identity range. Like cluster ID 0, we would use the first 256 IDs from each cluster range for those reserved/well-known identities. As the ingress identity seems the main concern among all the reserved / well known identity we could potentially restrict the scope of this change to only the ingress identity. This approach was mostly suggested by @squeed and @joestringer during the community meeting on the 11th of March (and I then took some time to open this mostly because of KubeCon 😅). **Notify relevant community channels** - @cilium/sig-policy - @cilium/sig-clustermesh **(Optional) Describe your proposed solution** Here are a few work streams/problems that we would need to solve (this is mostly me filing the blanks and discovering the future issues that we might have but it is potentially not exhaustive): 1) ID reservation We currently reserve the first 256 IDs only for cluster 0 -> https://github.com/cilium/cilium/blob/50d46815862602a849c2a060f6f629820a0bfa27/pkg/identity/numericidentity.go#L355 :(. What we could potentially do here is start changing the allocation code so that it never hands out new identities in that range (the linked function appears to be used for validation too, so we would need to introduce a new function and change specifically the allocation logic). In the long run, this should help empty that range. Depending on how confident we are with this part of the change, we could potentially backport it to all/some stable versions to increase the chance that those IDs would be mostly empty by the time users upgrade on a version where we actually start using those. When we start to actually use those IDs, we could have a preflight check that fails if there are still allocated IDs, and some command/instructions to spot the remaining identities that should be rotated. For instance, we could have some script/command that helps trace back the identity to the top-most resource (like Deployment/sts/ds/...) which should then be rolled out with new labels in its pods. A rollout like this should be safe netpol wise, and most Kubernetes users should be accustomed to such rollouts for Kubernetes version upgrades among other things. Note that this would only affect cluster with an ID different than 0. 2) Start using the new identity numeric IDs We should start to actually make the cluster ID influence the numeric ID of all reserved / well-known identities (or only the ingress identity if we restrict the scope to this only) and include the cluster label in the identity labels for the reserved identities. Only the identity should change, and probably not the underlying selector behind the entities, as we probably do not want to break existing network policies that select all clusters (we might (?) discuss doing this later on, but it is probably better not to mix that topic right now). Besides that, I do not really know how much of this can be done in a non-disruptive way (and whether it is actually possible to do it in a non-disruptive way at all). For instance, for the ingress identity, it might be possible to make it essentially like a pod rollout and keep both identities while starting to use the new one "gracefully" (since the envoy pod is separated from the cilium-agent it might be an actual pod rollout, but this might not work in practice ~). 3) Make remote clusters understand those new identities Currently, there is no actual CiliumIdentity created for those reserved/well-known identities and since it is currently the same identity for every cluster it just "works". But if we start using per-cluster identities for those, the remote cluster should actually know about them. In order to solve that, we could make each cluster create its own CiliumIdentity objects (in k8s or kvstore) for reserved/well-known identities. Alternatively, we could allocate the identities locally for each connected cluster, but this would make forward compatibility very hard when we start using those per-cluster reserved numeric identities and even anytime we introduce new identities. So this does not seem viable. Another choice could be to inject "fake" identities at the clustermesh-apiserver level because we only read this data from remote clusters, but unfortunately this does not work when kvstore is used because in that case kvstore is read from both the local cluster and remote clusters :(. So if we were to do this we would still need to actually create the CiliumIdentity objects in kvstore mode... 4) Cluster Mesh cleanups Once we have done everything above, we could probably start to not accept identities/endpoints in the 0-256 range from clusters which are not cluster 0. This should probably be done in a minor release after everything above was released to make version upgrades smooth (note that Cluster Mesh supports only 1 minor version skew). ----- This is mostly outside my main area of expertise, so I would gladly help with adjacent things if needed (like problems 1 and 4 here), but otherwise I am looking for someone who knows this a little better than me for the main policy changes 😅 🙏.

signal.title: feat(hubble/metrics): add path template matcher for the HTTP path label
signal.text: First PR of the CFP-26521 stack. Adds `pkg/hubble/metrics/pathtemplate`, which matches an HTTP request path against templates from the config and returns the template that matched. Returning the template rather than the path is what bounds the cardinality of the `path` label that later PRs add to the Hubble HTTP metrics, and is what resolves the objection this issue was originally closed on. Nothing is wired up yet, so there is no metric or behaviour change. Config plumbing, the handler, and Helm plus docs follow. Per the CFP: `{name}` and `{name...}` placeholders as `net/http.ServeMux` accepts them, templates tried in configured order with the first match winning, and a cap of 100 templates. Two notes for review: - `Match` splits a path only as far as the longest template can distinguish. The path is client controlled and Cilium does not set `max_request_headers_kb`, so Envoy's 60 KiB default applies. A 4000 slash path costs 26ns and no allocations instead of 32us and 65KB. - `Matcher.Shadowed()` has no caller yet. The watcher PR uses it to warn when an earlier template makes a later one unreachable, which a hit/miss counter cannot detect on its own. AIL: 2 Related: #26521 ```release-note Add the internal path template matcher that later PRs use to emit a bounded `path` label on the Hubble HTTP metrics. No user-facing change on its own. ```

signal.title: Feature request: add an option to supply more entropy for fib_lookup & fib_redirect
signal.text: ### Is your proposed feature related to a problem? Cilium's bpf functions that call fib_lookup or fib_redirect, e.g. [nodeport_rev_dnat_ipv6](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/blob/main/bpf/lib/nodeport.h#L948), seem to never pass src and dst ports (as well as flowlabels for ipv6 and so on) as a part of `struct bpf_fib_lookup` [url](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/blob/main/bpf/include/linux/bpf.h#L6974), which perfectly supports them. Although this may seem an overkill, consider the following setup: 1. A server, which is configured to use multipath routing via different interfaces with same ip addresses 2. Some client with large amount of traffic coming from a network behind NAT 3. LoadBalancer used with DSR enabled In this case only one interface will be used for egress as the values supplied for the kernel `fib6_table_lookup()` function hash-based nexthop selection will always be the same: the LB address and the client NAT address. That way the server equipped with multiple interfaces will be limited to the bandwith of only one of them for egress traffic. _P.S. I verified the above both by `bpftrace`-ing `bpf_ipv6_fib_lookup` & `fib6_table_lookup` and by manually suppling some additional entropy by mangling source ips_ ### Describe the feature you'd like I believe a simple configuration option alongside with not-so-heavy code changes conditionally passing more params to `bpf_fib_lookup` would do the trick. I personally believe this is not a good "first issue", but I would be glad to implement this myself if anyone has enough patience to go through reviewing everything. ### Notify relevant community channels _No response_ ### (Optional) Describe your proposed solution _No response_

signal.title: images/builder: Base on Ubuntu directly instead of the runtime image
signal.text: Currently, both the cilium-agent and the cilium-builder images are based on the same shared cilium-runtime base. This is causing challenges because those two images have different destinations: * The cilium-agent image is meant to be running in production, hence we want it to be as slim and light as possible (see #47065) * The cilium-builder image is used in CI and development environments and as such is not optimized to be light but rather to be quite full, including exhaustive cross-arch compiler toolchains and various utils tools This situation makes the common cilium-runtime base awkward: when we want to optimize the cilium-agent image, the leverage is at the source, but attempts to shrink the cilium-runtime base to achieve gains on the cilium-agent image cause problems for the cilium-builder image that needs what we want to remove from the cilium-agent image. A concrete example of that situation can be observed in PR #46446: That PR aims to remove the package manager suite from the cilium-agent image. In order to achieve that, it removes it at the source in the cilium-runtime image. But doing so breaks the cilium-builder image that does need a package manager. In order to unblock this situation, this PR changes the base of the cilium-builder image from the cilium-runtime image to a regular ubuntu base image. That way the cilium-runtime becomes only the base for the cilium-agent image and we can start applying slim-down optimizations there. This change is possible because the cilium-builder did not actually require most of what the cilium-runtime image adds on top of its ubuntu base. The only additional needed components is the `clang` binary that is transferred from the pre-built LLVM image. With this PR, the cilium-builder image no longer contains the following components: * iptables * iproute2 * ipset * kmod * gops * the CNI loopback plugin * the iptables-wrapper * libatomic1 * bash-completion * llc I combed through the various CI steps that use the builder image and local development make targets and I don't think any of those need any of the above. Along with that change, the `extract-llvm.sh` script used in CI to extract the LLVM toolchain gets updated to directly get it out of the cilium-llvm image instead of going through the cilium-builder one as a proxy.

signal.title: ipam/eni: Source the ENI VPC CIDRs from IMDS
signal.text: Today every ENI's status carries its VPC's CIDRs (`status.eni.enis.[].vpc`). But all ENIs for a given node can only belong to a single VPC, the node's VPC, so there is unnecessary duplication in having the VPC properties be present on each ENI's status. But in addition to that, we don't even need this to be in the `CiliumNode` CRD at all. Today the operator makes AWS EC2 API calls to get VPC CIDRs, then writes them to each ENI's status on the `CiliumNode` and the agent watches those on startup and waits to see them populated by the operator. The operator never reads those, only the agent needs them. And the agent doesn't even need the operator to get them. The agent already queries its node's IMDS for some node properties (including its VPC ID), we can just extend this IMDS-based facts gathering to get the agent the VPC CIDRs (which are available via IMDS). That way the agent no longer needs to wait for the operator to write those in the `CiliumNode` and the operator no longer needs to make AWS API calls to regularly fetch VPC properties. This PR implements the first half of that: update the agent to read the VPC CIDRs from the IMDS instead of from the operator-populated `CiliumNode`. The operator continues to fetch VPC data and write it to the `CiliumNode`, this is now advertised as deprecated and will be removed with cilium 1.22. See each commit message for details. signal.title: node: fix CiliumNode retaining a stale node IP when the address changes after agent startup
signal.text: Changes to the node's addresses never reached the LocalNodeStore and the agent kept the IP it read at init. If the kubelet published a stale address at agent start, CiliumNode kept the old IP. In syncFromK8s, compare and adopt the node IPs. An absent family is skipped: on a v4- or v6-only cluster the other family is legitimately nil. Fixes: #15406, #17500 ```release-note Fix CiliumNode retaining a stale node IP when the address changes after agent startup. ``` This PR was prepared with AIL:4. I personally validated the before and after results. My system is IPv6-first with IPv4. The IPv4 address is semi-stable by DHCP (will eventually expire if not renewed) but a new IPv6 is chosen with SLAAC on every boot. On boot the Kubelet initially publishes a stale IP that is then updated, but in the original code CiliumNode kept the stale IP, causing Cilium to not come up on reboot. Following this change and a similar one to cilium-health (next PR) reboots now work with no errors.

[`v1.10.0`](https://redirect.github.com/sirupsen/logrus/releases/tag/v1.10.0) [Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/sirupsen/logrus/compare/v1.9.4...v1.10.0) ### Logrus v1.10.0 This release focuses on substantial performance improvements, concurrency correctness, and better interoperability with modern Go logging APIs. #### 🚀 Performance Major improvements across `TextFormatter`, entry handling, and common logger paths: - \~17% lower geomean runtime across the benchmark suite - \~27% higher geomean formatter throughput - Common enabled logging paths are \~30–44% faster - `WithError` is \~40% faster - Chained fields are \~46% faster - `TextFormatter` paths are up to \~40% faster - Allocation counts are reduced by \~25–74% across measured `TextFormatter` cases, with the largest reductions in colored output The improvements also show up in complete logger paths: - Logger + `TextFormatter` is \~31% faster, with \~24% fewer allocations - Logger + `JSONFormatter` is \~21% faster, with \~10% fewer allocations `JSONFormatter` itself remains largely unchanged in runtime performance, with small allocation reductions. #### 🔄 `log/slog` interoperability v1.10 adds bidirectional interoperability between Logrus and Go's `log/slog`: - A Logrus `slog` hook can forward existing Logrus entries to an `slog` logger. - `hooks/slog.NewHandler` implements `slog.Handler`, allowing `log/slog` records to use an existing Logrus logger and its hooks, formatter, and output. - The handler preserves levels, fields, groups, context, record timestamps, and optionally caller information. - Caller reporting is configured per handler, without requiring Logrus's logger-wide `ReportCaller` option. - Custom `slog` levels can be mapped to Logrus levels. - The hook and handler can be combined, providing a practical path for incrementally migrating from Logrus to `log/slog` without requiring an all-at-once transition. This allows applications to migrate their logging API and logging backend independently: existing Logrus call sites can start using an `slog` backend, while new `slog` code can continue using an established Logrus setup. #### 🔒 Concurrency & Correctness - Fix reentrant logging deadlocks, including logging from within `MarshalJSON` or formatter code. - Fix generic `Log`, `Logf`, `Logln`, and `LogFn` methods unexpectedly panicking when called with `PanicLevel`, contrary to their documented behavior. - Eliminate race conditions in entry and formatter paths. - Improve locking boundaries around formatters and hooks. #### ➕ Added - `TextFormatter` now automatically enables colors on Windows terminals with ANSI support, matching behavior on other platforms. - `Entry.Caller` can now be set explicitly and is preserved across derived entries. When caller reporting is enabled, Logrus only detects and populates caller information when none was provided, allowing custom caller detection and wrapper-aware logging without adding additional caller configuration APIs. - Add minimal, composable logging interfaces for each log level, allowing consumers to depend on narrower interfaces and making logging implementations easier to substitute or adapt. - Expand CI verification to include TinyGo and every cross-compile target reported by go tool dist list, improving coverage across alternative toolchains and platforms. #### ⚠️ Behavioral Changes - Minimum supported Go version is now **1.23**. - `TextFormatter` now renders `[]byte` as raw/quoted strings instead of numeric slices. If you relied on the previous slice-of-ints output, convert explicitly before logging. - `TextFormatter` now uses dim cyan for debug output and dim white for trace output in colorized TTY output. - `Entry.HasCaller` is now deprecated in favor of checking `Entry.Caller` directly. A `//go:fix inline` directive was added so existing uses can be updated automatically. - `MutexWrap`, which was unintentionally exposed as public API, is deprecated. It remains available as an alias for compatibility but should not be used directly. *** v1.10 is primarily a performance, correctness, and interoperability release with no intentional breaking public signal.title: ci: resolve renovate PR metadata in base image workflows
signal.text: The base image push step relied on github.event.pull_request metadata to detect Renovate-authored PRs and temporarily re-draft them before pushing follow-up image updates. The reason behind this is to prevent unnecessary notifications / reviews from users. These reviews should already be handled by `ciliumbot`. That works for pull_request_target runs, but not for the workflow_call path used by the Renovate branch workflows, where github.event.pull_request is unset. In that case pr_number and pr_author were empty, so the workflow skipped the re-draft logic. Since this usecase is the relevant one, this commit fixes this by falling back to resolving the PR from the branch name with `gh pr list --head` when PR metadata is missing. Use the short ref name for the non-PR path so the branch lookup matches correctly. Note: we need to accept both Renovate author formats: - `cilium-renovate[bot]` from PR webhook payloads - `app/cilium-renovate` from `gh pr list` GraphQL output See PR: https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/47950 and related [workflow run](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/actions/runs/31743959287/job/94593874945) that didn't draft the PR as intended. Fixes: https://github.com/cilium/cilium/pull/47364
